anchors.description: Standard US kitchen finished countertop height, 36 in (0.914 m), measured from the front top edge of the back counter over the base cabinet run down to the floor at the cabinet toe base.
anchors.visible_evidence: Continuous front edge of the wood base-cabinet counter run is clearly visible at mid-right; directly below it the same cabinet face descends to a toe-kick/floor line, with open tiled floor beneath and in front. The two chosen points are roughly vertically aligned on that same cabinet bay.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Standard 36 in counter height is a strong building convention; main uncertainty is exact pixel placement (~0.1 m in depth) and whether p2 lands on the toe-kick face instead of the floor, slightly shortening the true distance.

anchors.description: One edge length of a standard 12 in x 12 in (0.305 m) glazed ceramic kitchen floor tile, between two adjacent grout-line intersections of the same tile in the open floor area.
anchors.visible_evidence: Large square floor tiles with dark grout lines in a diagonal layout are plainly visible on the open floor between the peninsula and the back cabinet run; the two points sit on adjacent grout intersections along one tile edge.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Tile format could be 12 in, 16 in or 18 in (0.30-0.46 m) glazed ceramic; the diagonal layout makes exact grout-junction placement at this resolution uncertain, hence the broad interval.

anchors.description: Height of a standard ceramic coffee mug, about 3.75 in (0.095 m), from its base on the countertop to the top rim.
anchors.visible_evidence: A white cylindrical handled mug stands upright on the counter left of the espresso machine; its base contact and top rim are both visible against the counter/wall background.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Object is clearly a mug-shaped vessel but could be a taller cup or small pitcher (up to ~0.12 m); small pixel span (~22 px) adds placement error.
